key_insight: PoreML is an open-source, pore-scale learning framework that combines GPU-based simulation data, large-scale datasets, and unified evaluation to predict multiphase flow in porous media.
engineering_relevance: It can help improve design and optimization of technologies such as CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging by enabling faster, physics-aware forecasting of pore-scale fluid behavior.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible data generation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across four scenarios
Unified training and evaluation for one-step prediction and autoregressive rollouts
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against analytical solutions and experiments, plus domain-specific protocols that test accuracy, physical consistency, and transfer to larger or micro-CT-derived domains.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on data coverage and generalization may be limited when transferring to unseen geometries, wetting conditions, or viscosity ratios.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
